'''Corinne Le Quéré'''<ref name=CBE/> {{post-nominals|country=CAN|CBE|FRS}} (born July 1966) is a Canadian scientist. She is Royal Society Research Professor of Climate Change Science at the [[University of East Anglia]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.uea.ac.uk/c_lequere |title= Corinne Le Quéré web page |publisher=University of East Anglia (UEA)|access-date=2021-03-21}}</ref> and former Director of [[Tyndall Centre|Tyndall Centre for Climate Change Research]]. She was the founding chair of the French [[High Council on Climate]] (2018-2024) and is a member of the UK [[Climate Change Committee]] since 2016. Her research focuses on the interactions between the [[carbon cycle]] and [[climate change]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://publons.com/researcher/1359497/corinne-le-quere |title= Research publications of Corinne Le Quéré |publisher=Publons|access-date=2021-03-21}}</ref>

==Education==
Le Quéré received her B.Sc. in physics from [[Université de Montréal|University of Montreal]], an M.S. in Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences from [[McGill University]], and a Ph.D. in oceanography from [[Pierre-and-Marie-Curie University|University of Paris VI]].<ref name="tyndall1">{{cite web|url=http://www.tyndall.ac.uk/people/corinne-le-quere |title=Corinne Le Quere Biography |website=Tyndall.ac.uk |access-date=2016-12-23}}</ref>

== Personal and early life ==
Le Quéré was born in Quebec in 1966 and as a child spent her camping holidays in the national parks of Eastern Canada which fostered her interest in the natural world.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=BBC Radio 4 - Desert Island Discs, Professor Corinne Le Quéré, climate scientist |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m001hnx7 |access-date=2023-02-03 |website=BBC |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=The Hot List: Meet Corinne Le Quéré, a woman at top of climate science |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/climate-change-scientists-lequere/ |access-date=2023-02-03}}</ref> She completed high school in 1984 and enrolled  for a course in general studies at the [[University of Ottawa]], near to her home in [[Gatineau]], prior to transferring to the [[University of Montreal]] to study physics.<ref name=":1" />

Le Quéré later became a British Citizen and holds both French and Canadian passports. She is now married to her second husband and has a daughter from her first marriage, Marianne, who she raised partly as a single mother.<ref name=":1" />

On 3 February 2023, Le Quéré was a guest on [[Desert Island Discs|BBC's Desert Island Discs]] on [[BBC Radio 4|Radio 4]] (presented by [[Lauren Laverne]]). As an imaginary [[Castaway]] she chose a mask and snorkel as her luxury items and, for her favourite disc, ''[[La Vida Es Un Carnaval]] by [[Celia Cruz]].'' For her book, she chose [[World Atlas of the Oceans]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dave Monahan > Compare Discount Book Prices & Save up to 90% > ISBNS.net |url=https://www.isbns.net/author/Dave_Monahan |access-date=2023-02-04 |website=www.isbns.net}}</ref> by Dave Monahan.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Desert Island Discs |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/programme/b-prderl/desert-island-discs/episodes/ |access-date=2023-02-03 |website=Radio Times |language=en}}</ref>

==Career and research==
She was co-chair of the [[Global Carbon Project]] (GCP) from 2009 until 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.globalcarbonproject.org |title=GCP : Global Carbon Project : Homepage |publisher=Global Carbon Project |access-date=2016-12-23}}</ref>  Within the GCP, she initiated and directed for over a decade the annual publication of the Global Carbon Budget.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.globalcarbonproject.org/carbonbudget |title=Carbon Budget |website=Globalcarbonproject.org |date=2016-11-14 |access-date=2016-12-23}}</ref><ref>[[IPCC Fifth Assessment Report]], for which Dr. Le Quéré is a lead author.</ref> During 2014-2017 she has been a member of the Scientific Committee of the Future Earth platform for sustainability research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.futureearth.org/ |title=Home |publisher=Future Earth |access-date=2016-12-23}}</ref><ref name="tyndall1"/> She is author of the 3rd, 4th and 5th assessment reports of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]]. She conducted research at [[Princeton University]] in the US (1992–1996), at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry]] in Germany (2000–2005), and jointly between the UEA and the [[British Antarctic Survey]] in the UK (2005–2010).

==Honours and awards==

In 2012, Le Quéré was awarded the Claude Berthault award from the French Academy of Sciences,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/activite/prix/laureat_berthault.pdf |title=Prix de Mme Claude Berthault: Lauréat d'année 2014 |access-date=2015-02-09 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150209172424/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/activite/prix/laureat_berthault.pdf |archive-date=2015-02-09 }}</ref> the first Copernicus medal of the Copernicus Gesellschaft e.V. in 2013/2014,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.copernicus-gesellschaft.org/medal.html |title=Copernicus e.V. - Medal |website=Copernicus-gesellschaft.org |access-date=2016-12-23}}</ref> and was the annual Bolin lecturer in Stockholm University in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.science.su.se/english/about-us/calendar/science-forum-with-prof-corinne-le-qu%C3%A9r%C3%A9-bolin-climate-lecturer-2014-1.168535 |title=Science Forum with Prof. Corinne Le Quéré, Bolin Climate Lecturer 2014 - Faculty of Science |website=Science.su.se |access-date=2016-12-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531141158/http://www.science.su.se/english/about-us/calendar/science-forum-with-prof-corinne-le-qu%C3%A9r%C3%A9-bolin-climate-lecturer-2014-1.168535 |archive-date=2016-05-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2015, she received a Blaise Pascal Medal for Earth and Environmental Sciences from the European Academy of Sciences<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.eurasc.org/medals/pb_medals_15.asp |title=The Blaise Pascal Medals 2015 |access-date=2018-01-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113150306/http://www.eurasc.org/medals/pb_medals_15.asp |archive-date=2018-01-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the Grande Médaille Albert 1er de Monaco, Science section.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oceano.org/prix-et-medailles/laureat-medailles/ |title=Grande médailles |publisher=Institut Océanographique, Fondation Albert 1er, Prince de Monaco |access-date=2021-03-22}}</ref>

In 2016, Le Quéré was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/corinne-le-quere-12881/ |title=Corinne Le Quéré |publisher=Royal Society |access-date=2016-12-23}}</ref>

In 2019, Le Quéré was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2019 Birthday Honours]] for services to climate change science.<ref name=CBE>{{London Gazette|issue=62666|supp=y|page=B9|date=8 June 2019}}</ref>

In 2019, she also won the [[Prince Albert I Medal]]<ref>http://iapso.iugg.org/awards-and-honors/the-prince-albert-i-medal25.html {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514080904/https://iapso.iugg.org/awards-and-honors/the-prince-albert-i-medal25.html |date=14 May 2021 }} Prince Albert I Medal</ref> and was made a {{lang|fr|Chevalier}} of the French [[Legion of Honour]].<ref>{{Citation |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/WAspad/UnTexteDeJorf?numjo=PRER1910335D |title=Loi n° PRER1910335D du 13 juillet 2019 portant promotion et nomination |language=fr |work=[[Journal Officiel de la République Française]] |date=14 July 2019 }}</ref>

In 2020, she received the [[Heineken Prize]] for Environmental Sciences for her interdisciplinary research on the interactions between climate change and the [[carbon cycle]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uea.ac.uk/about/-/uea-professor-wins-international-environmental-sciences-prize-for-climate-change-research |title=UEA professor wins international environmental sciences prize for climate change research |publisher=[[University of East Anglia]] |date=3 June 2020 |access-date=3 June 2020 }}</ref>

In 2025, she received the Vladimir Ivanovich Vernadsky Medal <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.egu.eu/awards-medals/vladimir-ivanovich-vernadsky/2025/corinne-le-quere |title=Vladimir Ivanovich Vernadsky Medal : Homepage |publisher=European Geosciences Union |access-date=2016-12-23}}</ref> of the [[European Geosciences Union]]. 

She was awarded an honorary doctorate from Utrecht University (2023) and from the Université de Montréal (2025). 

==Selected publications==
A full list of Le Quéré's peer-reviewed publications can be found on her Publons profile.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://publons.com/researcher/1359497/corinne-le-quere |title= Research publications of Corinne Le Quéré |publisher=Publons|access-date=2021-03-21}}</ref>
* Economy-wide but fragile decreases in greenhouse gas emissions supported by climate policy in France (2025). Le Quéré, C., Comptes Rendus Geoscience, 357, 503-516. https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/geoscience/articles/10.5802/crgeos.311/
* Fossil CO<sub>2</sub> emissions in the post-COVID-19 era (2021). Le Quéré, C. et al., Nature Climate Change, 11, 197–199, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-021-01001-0.
* Emerging climate impact on carbon sinks in a consolidated carbon budget. Friedlingstein, P., Le Quéré, C., et al. (2026). Nature, 649, 98-103. https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09802-5
* Decreasing importance of carbon-climate feedbacks in the Southern Ocean in a warming climate. Jarnikova, T., Le Quéré, C., Rumbold, S., & Jones, C. (2025). Science Advances, 11(20), eadr3589. https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adr3589
* Temporary reduction in daily global CO<sub>2</sub> emissions during the COVID-19 forced confinement. Le Quéré, C. et al (2020). Nature Climate Change, 10, 647-653. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-020-0797-x
* Drivers of declining CO<sub>2</sub> emissions in 18 developed economies. Le Quéré, C. et al. (2019). Nature Climate Change, 9, 213-217. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-019-0419-7
* Role of zooplankton dynamics for Southern Ocean phytoplankton biomass and global biogeochemical cycles. Le Quéré, C. et al. (2016). Biogeosciences 13, 4111–4133. https://doi.org/10.5194/bg-13-4111-2016
* The Global Carbon Budget 1959-2011. Le Quéré, C., and 31 others (2013), Earth System Science Data (ESSD), 5, 165-186. https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/5/165/2013/
* Ecosystem dynamics based on plankton functional types for global ocean biogeochemistry models. Le Quéré, C., and 9 others (2005). Global Change Biology, 11, 2016-2040. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2486.2005.1004.x
* Oceanic carbon dioxide uptake in a model of century-scale global warming. Sarmiento, J.L. and C. Le Quéré (1996). Science, 274, 1346-1350. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.274.5291.1346
